reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited paragraphs support it: Section 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) contains only compliance, notification, access-restriction and anti-spam obligations, and Section 10 is limited to information protection — no 'shall not solicit', 'employ or engage', 'no-hire' or inducement language binding the Client appears anywhere in the supplied text.

This matches the playbook's preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer'), so no redline or counterparty comment is warranted; the proposal correctly leaves the text unchanged and offers no comment.

The two failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are content constraints that only apply where a non-solicit exists; satisfying them would require inserting a restrictive covenant against our own client, which would be a directionally wrong edit. Treating them as inapplicable is the correct reading.

The rationale appropriately flags the fallback/walk-away positions for future negotiation and notes the separately-papered Non-Competition Agreement referenced in § 8(d) as an out-of-document diligence item, which does not undermine the in-document compliance conclusion.
